cohort: 3193 pregnant women who delivered at a tertiary care center in Nepal between September 15, 2019 and October 15, 2020
finding: The prevalence of cesarean delivery at a tertiary care center in Nepal was found to be higher than the World Health Organization's recommendations, with fetal distress being the leading indication.
mod_finding: Transient tachypnea of newborns was more common in neonates delivered via elective cesarean section (60.46%) compared to emergency cesarean section (44.28%).
